title: Sampling for longtail errors — triage & heuristics
content:
Purpose: quick reference + sandbox for how we pick samples from long-tail failures for human review. Not a final policy — notes for discussion with QA and ML ops.

Problem framing:
- We see a long tail of rare label errors (0.1-1% frequency) that nonetheless cause Q/A regressions in production prompts. Expensive to surface by random sampling.
- Need a lightweight sampling + priority scheme so humans see high-signal rare failures without blowing up review budget.

Constraints / targets:
- Review budget: ~500 examples / week for ad-hoc triage squad.
- Want coverage across: model versions, user-visible routes, languages (EN, FR, ES), and entity types.
- Prefer short lifecycle: triage -> quick fix or routing to deep-investigation.

Candidate signals (ranked):
1) Regression-delta: examples where current model output diverged from gold or previous model on same prompt (high precision).
2) Low-confidence + high-length generation: model confidence proxies (token-prob avg < threshold) for >128 token outputs.
3) Rare label patterns: label categories with freq <0.05% in training sample (e.g., multi-span nested dates).
4) User escalations / CS tickets (high priority).
5) Metric spikes (per-route error rate spike > 2x baseline in last 24h).

Sampling recipe (draft):
- Allocate weekly slots: 200 regression-delta, 150 low-confidence-long, 75 rare-pattern, 50 CS escalations, reserve 25 ad-hoc.
- Within each bucket, stratify by model-version and route so we don't over-sample from one route.
- Max 20 examples per user to avoid bias.

Heuristics for dedup / noise filtering:
- Collapse near-duplicates: same prompt text + identical golden label => keep one sample.
- If prompt contains PII tokens (SSN-like, long hashes), route to secure-review only.
- Automatic discard: obvious formatting problems (truncated HTML, very short token counts <3) unless flagged by CS.

Quick triage rubric (sticky notes for reviewer):
- 1) Reproducible? Try 3 seeds / temp values. If failure inconsistent, mark "probabilistic".
- 2) Label error vs model hallucination? If label is clearly wrong -> tag "label-bad" and add suggested corrected label.
- 3) Edge-case policy gap? (e.g., ambiguous spans, nested entities) tag "policy-gap" and add minimal repro prompt.
- 4) Action: quick-fix (update heuristic/tagging), escalate to label team (relabel batch), escalation to model team (pattern needs model change).

Examples (toy rows for reviewer UI):
- id: 987532, route: chat/compose, model: rdlw-v2.1, signal: regression-delta, issue: nested-date parsed as two entities ("May 5" and "5 May 2022"), suggestion: merge spans into single normalized date.
- id: 994021, route: embeddings/search, model: rdlw-embed-1, signal: rare-pattern, issue: product codes mis-classified as person names when preceded by "attn:".
- id: 100112, route: hosted-api/generate, model: rdlw-v2.0, signal: low-conf-long, issue: irrelevant tangential ramble after safe content, label: topic-coherence-fail.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Threshold tuning: what token-prob avg threshold gives 80% precision for low-confidence heuristic? Run A/B on 2 weeks of logs. (ticket AI-4402)
- Should CS escalations bypass buckets? right now they are a small reserved slot; maybe increase.
- Produce a small dashboard (per-bucket precision/recall) — link to dashboard ticket in /ops.
- Need strict PII handling SOP in this doc: currently vague. Follow up with Security.

Notes to self:
- Try running a weekend pass pulling 2k candidates, label 200 to estimate precision per-signal.
- Collaborators: ping Riley for stratified sampler code, Alexei for reviewer rubric sync.

Slack refs / historical context: see thread #label-qc on 2024-09-18 (notes from retro). Also relates to "label-cleanup-heuristic-cookbook" but different scope (this is sampling, not heuristics bank).

Quick links (for triage sheet):
- PR with sampler code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-tools/pull/218
- Core label QA playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Label+QA+Playbook

If we want to formalize: convert this into a 1-page policy + simple sampler script (python) that outputs weekly CSV for reviewers. For now: this is the running notebook / notes.
